verdict.rationale: Highnote documents platform-enforced spend rules on dollar amount and authorization count. Velocity controls add time windows to those rules, shown with a weekly $1,000 example. Rules can be set at the card, account, or program level and are evaluated at authorization, before funds move. missing for 10: explicit documentation of daily, monthly, and all-time windows (only a weekly example is shown); explicit per-cardholder (account-holder) scoping, since only card, account, and program levels are named; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can set spend limits per card and per cardholder — amount caps over daily, monthly, or all-time windows, and transaction-count velocity rules — enforced by the platform, not my code

citations.quote: You can configure that logic on merchant category codes (MCC), dollar amount, authorization count, and more.
Velocity controls allow time boundary constraints to be applied to a spend rule.
This creates a velocity control that enforces a weekly spending limit of $1,000.
Set velocity limits, merchant category restrictions, and per-transaction caps at the card, account, or program level. Every rule is evaluated at authorization, before funds move.
